- Antibiotics will start today — even if cultures are pending.  
- Strict weight-bearing restriction on the right leg until further evaluation.  
- Return immediately for fever, chills, worsening pain/swelling, or inability to move toes/foot (nerve compromise).

The clinical presentation centers on an acute, non-traumatic right knee monoarthritis with high suspicion for septic arthritis — the leading concern based on urgency, clinical impression, and recommended empiric IV antibiotics. No imaging findings (e.g., osteomyelitis, soft tissue gas), no immunocompromised state, no prosthetic joint, and no reported fever or leukocytosis are mentioned — but their absence does not negate septic arthritis, which can present with subtle systemic signs. The urgent management plan (IV antibiotics, repeat synovial culture, ortho consult for possible surgical drainage) aligns exclusively with septic arthritis as the working diagnosis driving action.

- Acute non-traumatic right knee monoarthritis  
- Clinical impression explicitly states “highly concerning for septic arthritis”  
- Empiric IV antibiotics (vancomycin + ceftriaxone) initiated — standard for suspected native-joint septic arthritis

- Orthopedic consultation considered for surgical irrigation/debridement — definitive management for septic arthritis when indicated  
- Patient counseled about signs of worsening infection (fever, chills, neurologic compromise) — consistent with infectious urgency  

[GAPS]  
- Synovial fluid WBC count and differential (critical for differentiating septic vs. crystal arthritis)  
- Synovial fluid glucose level (low glucose supports septic arthritis)  
- Blood cultures result (pending)  
- CRP and ESR values (pending)  
- Synovial fluid Gram stain result (not mentioned — would provide rapid clue to bacterial etiology)  
- Fever or vital sign abnormalities (not specified)  
- Presence/absence of overlying cellulitis or skin breach (not described)  

[DIAGNOSIS]  
Septic arthritis
